messages:
incident-bot: PAGER -> prod: elevated latency and token drop observed on streaming endpoints /v1/chat/stream (us-west-2). auto-alert triggered at 1968240000. p95 latency spiked from 220ms -> 1.8s; throughput (tokens/sec) down ~40%. tagging as SEV2.

sara nguyen: I'm on it. seeing lots of partial frames + connection churn in traces. opening dashboards now.

daniel park: what's the initial hypothesis? kernel scheduling on GPU nodes or a sudden workload shift (lots of long-context streams)?

maria lopez: metrics look like continuous-batching backlog growth. KV cache hit-rate unchanged, but queues for streamer-workers are backing up. heatmap shows 70% of stream sessions are >512 tokens.

sara nguyen: immediate mitigation options: 1) rate-limit streaming requests by route 2) reduce max stream length 3) temporarily turn off streaming responses (fall back to poll/batched non-stream) for lower tiers/customers. which to do now?

kevin chung: favor option 3 for fastest recovery. toggling streaming off is a single FF flip for gateway and runtime and will let us shed tail latency quickly. downside: UX regressions for customers relying on SSE.

daniel park: agree. do non-breaking fallback first: toggled only for non-enterprise and anonymous keys. keep enterprise and dedicated on.

sara nguyen: working on FF toggle. patch looks like:```bash
# feature-flag service
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggles/streaming -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"value":"off","scope":"non_enterprise:all"}'
```

maria lopez: I'll push a transient rate-cap too, just in case. adding a per-key token-rate limit of 0.6x for streaming endpoints so new arrivals don't overload the backlog; will keep it until streaming is healthy.

ops-bot: Deploy started: feature-flags/disable-streaming-nonent -> infra-canary (sha: a1b2c3d). CI passed.

ops-bot: Deploy finished: feature-flags/disable-streaming-nonent -> infra-canary (sha: a1b2c3d).

sara nguyen: Toggle applied. Confirming: non-enterprise keys now receive the non-streaming response path (short-poll). Observed immediate drop in streaming connections by ~32%.

maria lopez: p95 latency now down to 320ms and tokens/sec throughput recovered to ~95% of baseline. queues draining. We still have a small number of long live streams on enterprise tier — those are healthy.

kevin chung: customer impact: small percentage of free-tier users see slower UX (no streaming) but API responses still complete. flagging support + status page. Any customers on paid plans?

sara nguyen: Quick check: only 3 mid-market customers using streaming in us-west-2; they are flagged as enterprise-equivalent so not impacted. No major enterprise customers affected so far.

daniel park: Open follow-ups: - run a background job to trim >2k token sessions where safe - add circuit-breaker on stream queue depth - roll a bugfix to improve continuous-batching scheduler for long contexts

maria lopez: I'll create the post-incident eval for model-serving with sample prompts that surface the issue. also keep streaming FF in place until next deploy validates scheduler changes.

ops-bot: incident ticket created: INC-2026-1927 (link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-2026-1927)

sara nguyen: Handoff: I'm going offline in 30m. handing to @lindsey (oncall-night). Lindsey — current state: streaming disabled for non-enterprise in us-west-2, rate-cap 0.6x in place, p95 back to ~320ms, queues draining. If we see re-acceleration of queue depth, escalate to runtime eng.

lindsey park (oncall-night): Acked. I'll watch for rebound and keep paging cadence at 15m. Please pin the FF rollback command in the ticket so I can revert if we overcorrect.

daniel park: rollback snippet (to revert streaming for non-entire scope):```bash
curl -X POST https://flags.redwood.internal/api/toggles/streaming -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" -d '{"value":"on","scope":"non_enterprise:all"}'
```

sara nguyen: Thanks team — logging actions in the incident doc. I'll add customer-facing note for status.page explaining temporary switch to non-streaming on free tier.

maria lopez: leaving diagnostics collection running for 24h. will attach KV cache and batcher traces to the ticket.

incident-bot: SEV2 -> acknowledged by sara nguyen. next update scheduled in 15 minutes.
